card.name: Balos
card.tagline: A vigorous, three-part paired folk dance from the island of Kythnos, Greece.
card.profile: Balos, or Thermiotikos Balos, is a traditional folk dance from the island of Kythnos, Greece. It is a vigorous, three-part paired dance performed by men and women during local festivals, typically following the sirto. The dance is distinguished by its continuous back-to-back rotations, known as 'voltes' or 'furles,' which require significant coordination between partners.
card.insight: The Kythnos Balos is defined by 'voltes' or 'furles,' where partners perform continuous back-to-back rotations while holding hands, a technique noted by choreographers like Dora Stratou for its technical demand.
sources: Source: Balos (Greek dance) on Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0. Read: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balos_(Greek_dance)
card.profile_long: The Balos of Kythnos, also known as the Thermiotikos Balos, represents a distinct branch of the Greek island dance tradition. Unlike the versions of Balos found elsewhere in the Aegean, the Kythnos variant is characterized by a specific technical intensity and a structure composed of three distinct parts. It is an integral component of the cultural life of the island, serving as a staple of local festivals and summer events. Traditionally, the dance is performed following the sirto, creating a sequence that is central to the island's musical and choreographic heritage. The dance is performed in pairs, with both men and women participating. The defining movement of the dance involves the couple holding hands while executing continuous, rapid rotations. These rotations, performed back-to-back around their own axes and simultaneously around their partner, are referred to locally as 'voltes' or 'furles.' This specific movement pattern has been the subject of study by prominent Greek musicologists and choreographers, including Dora Stratou and Domna Samiou, who identified the dance as particularly demanding. The dance remains a living tradition, maintained through the community festivals of Kythnos.

sections.how_it_is_danced: The dance is a paired, three-part performance. Participants hold hands and execute continuous rotations, moving back-to-back around their own axes and their partner's axis simultaneously.
sections.music_and_instruments: The dance is part of the music tradition of Kythnos and is performed following the sirto dance. Specific instrumentation is not described in sources.
sections.costume_and_setting: The dance is performed primarily during local festivals and summer events on the island of Kythnos.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: It is an integral part of the music and dance tradition of Kythnos, performed during local feasts and festivals.
sections.notable_figures: Dora Stratou and Domna Samiou are noted as having studied and highlighted the specificity and demanding nature of the dance.
sections.regional_variants: The Kythnos Balos is distinguished from other Balos dances found in the rest of the Greek islands by its unique execution and rotation techniques.
sections.lineage: The dance is traditionally linked to the sirto, which precedes it in the sequence of festival dances.
